additions.name: Huailai Smart Space AI Industrial Park (怀来县智慧空间人工智能产业园) — data-centre buildings 1#-6# with two 110 kV substations

status.summary: On 5 August 2026 the Huailai County Natural Resources and Planning Bureau published the construction-project planning verification and land verification (核字第2026Z006号, verification date 5 August 2026) of the Huailai Smart Space AI Industrial Park project (project code 2207-130730-89-01-769965), built by 华夏雅库(河北)网络科技有限公司 at 十八家村 and 小南辛堡村, Xiaonanxinpu town, under planning permits 建字第130730202400031号 and 建字第130730202400039号. The verified buildings are 1#-6# data centres, the fire-control centre and guard room, the underground fire-water pool and the No. 1 and No. 2 110 kV substations, with a buried oil-tank area. Planning verification checks completed works against the permit before completion acceptance, so completion of these buildings is recorded with that scope. Fit-out, commissioning, operation, operator and capacity are not established.

locator.precision: Area centroid of the red-line parcel GY22-46 (69,941.54 m2) drawn on the official site plan, registered to Esri World Imagery; it falls inside the 4# data-centre building. It locates the parcel of the six-building campus, not a particular building, entrance, survey point or construction extent.
locator.identity_review: The 5 August 2026 verification and the 1 April 2024 publicity name the same project, builder (华夏雅库) and villages. The 2024 site plan shows six data-centre buildings 1#-6# in three rows with the No. 1 110 kV substation at the west end of the middle row and the No. 2 substation at the south-west corner, exactly the buildings verified in 2026. The 2024 land-use analysis map places the parcel west of road Y127 and south of 葡萄大道, south of the G6 expressway and south-west of an industrial park. Esri imagery at that position shows a parallelogram campus with this unique layout. Eight building corners register the plan to the imagery with 2.4 m RMS, and the registered parcel area (70,461 m2) is within 0.7% of the stated 69,941.54 m2. The map's hand-drawn project box, registered separately (20 m RMS), lands on the same campus 44 m from the point. Details: sources/research-countries-2026-10-27-cn-hebei-tianjin-beijing-p5-huailai-smart-space-ai-park-geometry-facts.json.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The site plan states CGCS2000 but prints no coordinates, so the position rests on Esri imagery of unknown date and absolute accuracy; corner picking, roof displacement and drawing generalisation add unquantified error. The 2.4 m registration RMS and the decimal places are not ground accuracy.

additions.name: Volcano Engine Inner Mongolia Horinger Compute Centre Phase 1 A — 10-1 data-centre machine-room building

status.summary: On 27 October 2026 the Horinger New Area planning and construction bureau reported that the 10-1 data-centre machine-room building works of the Volcano Engine Inner Mongolia Horinger Compute Centre Phase 1 A project had recently completed their construction completion-acceptance filing (竣工验收备案). The works are the 10-1 machine-room building, 32,138.14 m2 of floor area, with a stated IT capacity of 26 MW. The record covers construction completion of building 10-1 only: operation is described as a future step and is not asserted, the 26 MW is a design figure and not installed load, and the other Phase 1 A machine-room buildings (10-2 to 10-4), the separately accepted integrated building, the 110 kV substation, Phase 1 B (10-5 to 10-8) and the separate Phase 2 park are not included.

locator.precision: EIA point of the Phase 1 A gas boiler house inside the integrated building, which lies at the north of the Phase 1 A parcel, immediately east of building 10-1. The point is inside the Phase 1 A parcel computed from its CGCS2000 parcel plan, 54 m from the parcel boundary and 155 m from the parcel centroid, and about 165 m east-north-east of the visual centre of building 10-1. It locates the Phase 1 A campus of the compute centre; it is not the footprint or centre of building 10-1, nor an entrance, and it does not locate Phase 1 B (east of Phase 1 A) or the separate Phase 2 park.
locator.identity_review: The Hohhot Ecology and Environment Bureau published the EIA report form with its acceptance notice of 18 June 2025 for the Volcano Engine Inner Mongolia Horinger Compute Centre Phase 1 project, built by Hohhot Saibei Hongcheng Technology Co., Ltd.; the report's boiler house heats the Phase 1 A integrated building and pump house and lies inside the Phase 1 project. Printed 111 deg 50 min 48.120 s E, 40 deg 35 min 9.456 s N and 111.84670, 40.58596, transcribed arithmetically. The earlier version of the same report appends the Horinger New Area filing notice (project code 2409-150123-89-01-454670; Phase 1 A 119,698.23 m2 with four machine-room buildings, the integrated building containing the boiler room and a 110 kV substation) and the Phase 1 A parcel plan on the 2000 national geodetic system: its ten boundary points (3-degree zone 37) reproduce all ten printed side lengths to within 1 mm and enclose 119,698.24 m2, equal to the filing's Phase 1 A area, and the EIA point lies inside that parcel; the GCJ-02 reading of the point would fall 584 m west, 297 m outside the parcel. Independently, the Phase 1 A 110 kV substation EIA (Inner Mongolia EED, 26 February 2025) places that station in the south-west corner of the Phase 1 A plant area, and its four printed corner points fall inside the computed parcel at its south-west corner. In independent Esri imagery the computed parcel follows the walled construction compound and the point falls on its north-east integrated-building block; the report's general layout puts building 10-1 immediately west of the boiler house. The 27 October 2026 status record names the same Phase 1 A project and building 10-1; the 10 August 2026 New Area item's 12 ha, four-building Phase 1 description matches Phase 1 A. Details: sources/research-countries-2026-10-27-cn-inner-mongolia-p5-volcano-horinger-phase-1a-geometry-facts.json.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The report states no datum or positional accuracy. The WGS84/CGCS2000 reading is supported by the point lying inside the Phase 1 A parcel computed from the parcel plan's CGCS2000 boundary coordinates and by the parcel's agreement with independent Esri imagery of unstated accuracy and date (manual visual comparison, roughly 10 m). The point marks the integrated-building block about 165 m from the centre of building 10-1. Decimal places are transcription precision, not accuracy.
